name: Helix
summary: Helix runs a 7B internet-pretrained VLM (S2) at 7-9 Hz producing a single latent vector, consumed by an 80M visuomotor transformer (S1) at 200 Hz that drives 35 upper-body degrees of freedom including individual fingers, wrists, head and torso. Both run on embedded GPUs in the robot. Figure demonstrated two Helix robots collaborating on grocery put-away with one set of weights and no task-specific fine-tuning.
innovation: Decoupled S1/S2 running at different rates, communicating through one learned latent vector.
Entirely onboard inference with no cloud dependency, at true servo rates.
A single weight set controlling multiple cooperating robots.
matters: Showed frontier-scale VLA behavior can fit inside a humanoid's power and latency budget.
limits: No paper, no weights, no external evaluation; claims rest on company demonstrations.
lineage: The VLA concept restructured for embedded real-time humanoid control.
